Martinstag Warm Spiced Cider

Served at: Martinstag Lantern Evening

Serves 6-8Prep 5 minCook 20 min

Warm Spiced Cider is a comforting beverage often enjoyed during Martinstag (St. Martin's Day) celebrations on November 11th, particularly in Germany and Austria. After the traditional lantern parades, families and children gather to warm up with this fragrant, non-alcoholic drink, perfect for chasing away the autumn chill.

Ingredients

  • 1 gallon (3.8 L) apple cider
  • 4-6 cinnamon sticks
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) whole cloves
  • 2-3 star anise pods (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (120 mL) brown sugar or maple syrup (adjust to taste)
  • 1 orange, thinly sliced or just the peel

Method

  1. Pour the apple cider into a large pot or Dutch oven.
  2. Add the cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, star anise (if using), and orange slices or peel to the pot.
  3. Stir in the brown sugar or maple syrup, starting with a smaller amount and adding more later if desired, depending on the sweetness of your cider.
  4. Heat the cider over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until it is hot and steaming but not boiling. Do not let it come to a rolling boil, as this can diminish the fresh apple flavor.
  5. Once hot, reduce the heat to low and let the cider simmer gently for at least 15-20 minutes to allow the spices to infuse their flavors.
  6. Carefully ladle the warm cider into heatproof mugs. You can strain out the spices and orange slices before serving, or leave them in for a rustic presentation.
  7. Garnish each mug with a fresh cinnamon stick or an orange slice, if desired, and serve immediately.

Tips

  • For an adult version, a shot of dark rum, brandy, or bourbon can be added to individual mugs after heating.
  • Keep the cider warm in a slow cooker on the 'warm' setting for larger gatherings or to enjoy throughout the evening.
  • Adjust the amount of sweetener and spices to your personal preference; taste and add more as needed.
